label: prop:self-dual-higgs-real-volume
title: The self-dual Higgs ($4_1$) has a real complex volume ($\mathrm{CS}=0$)
html:
The figure-eight knot 4_1 (the Higgs mass-scale motif) is strongly amphichiral, as tabulated by Dale Rolfsen [rolfsen] and analysed in complex Chern--Simons theory by Edward Witten [witten2011, §5.3]. Under the bar-involution \sigma\colon q \mapsto q^{-1}, its colored Jones polynomial is fixed:

  J_N(4_1; q) = J_N(4_1; q^{-1}) \qquad (\forall N).

Consequently, its Neumann--Zagier complex volume \mathbb{V}(4_1) = \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) + i\,\mathrm{CS}(4_1) of Walter D. Neumann and Don Zagier [neumann-zagier1985] (in the asymptotic colored-Jones normalisation of Rinat M. Kashaev [kashaev1997] and Hitoshi Murakami and Jun Murakami [murakami-murakami2001]) is real:

  \mathrm{CS}(4_1) = 0,
  \qquad
  \mathrm{Re}\,\mathbb{V}(4_1) = \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) \approx 2.0299.

The bare Higgs knot contributes only the real volume (mass) face. Its imaginary (decay) face vanishes, proving that \mathfrak{Q}_\beta is not a property of the lone Higgs knot.

For the amphichiral 4_1, its invariant trace field \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-3}) and invariant quaternion algebra are closed under complex conjugation by the necessary amphicheirality criterion of Walter D. Neumann and Alan W. Reid [neumann-reid, §3.2, Prop. 3.4], and both archimedean saddles (hyperbolic and torus) collapse onto the real axis. This self-duality is an algebraic identity over any commutative ring with a bar-involution.
